actual_scope: Proof note on the selected P104 record under a stated hypothesis ledger (H1-H6): the rank-mass surplus S = 760 = v(L-1) - Lc and a conditional upper bound S <= sum_p (L_p - 1) - sum_j c_j; the ratio lemma N >= 1 + dim ker(R+I) for words of isotropic rank-one units; a hub rank law (Theorem 4) in the coordinate-mask grammar; a form-capacity lemma (Theorem 5, ku >= v) for the stated one-pass stop family, with a numerical cross-check on small cells; a scoped typed-query proposition (a rank-one Q-odd unit has Bruhat rank one); and label corrections (package convention versus SPEC versus verifier behaviour). Arithmetic on stated invoice totals is retained and labelled as typed-in constants. No word is built and no kappa is claimed.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a joint helper basis and a legal causal split on the complete invoice. This package builds no word and prices no supplier; it states conditional structural bounds on the surplus numerator, a hub rank law and a capacity lemma for one stop family, each with its hypotheses, and keeps every open door at a named hypothesis.
bottleneck_link: docs/research/research-family-status.md; the statements bound the surplus numerator S and constrain the hub and helper-form structure of any word in the stated grammar. They say nothing about the denominator or about kappa.
stop_rule: No kappa claim and no new word. Open and stated: two hosted Q-odd units per LOCAL (H5); a cheaper realisation of thin queries (H6) and whether a shear-typed supplier can be priced below a rank-one leaf; c below 56 outside the Gram class; words with leak, in-place units, or exactness only in a limit; hub grammars other than coordinate masks with one scalar per LOCAL; Theorem 5 outside the stated stop shape (down-row landings at a line after X reached V, T[Y,Y] != 0, non-diagonal port Gram, rank-one crossings at mid frames).
evidence: README.md and THEOREM.md (statements, proofs, hypothesis ledger), check.py with checks/ (exact certificates over the rationals and one numpy-based numerical cross-check for Theorem 5) and data/ (selected-record profile, quoted-line table).

open_questions.question: Can a LOCAL host two Q-odd units per port (H5), and if so does any word reach the 2632 value that the same arithmetic allows?
open_questions.why_it_matters: H5 is a family assumption, not a consequence of rank conservation; Theorem 2 depends on it, and with two hosted units per LOCAL the surplus arithmetic would allow 2632.
open_questions.first_step: State the verifier conditions under which one LOCAL can contain two independent Q-odd units of one port path, then test whether rank conservation forbids it.
open_questions.blocked_by: No proof or counterexample either way; the hosted-unit count is only a family assumption.

open_questions.question: Can a shear-typed supplier realise the thin queries below one rank-one paid call per port (H6, shear exponent)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The bound S <= v(L-1) - Lc prices an unhosted Q-odd unit at one uncredited rank-one query; a cheaper accounting would raise the numerator bound.
open_questions.first_step: Decide whether the non-unitary shear factorisation C = U(i) W U(i), which lies outside the Clifford rank lemma, has a priced realisation below a leaf in the finite compiler's cost model.
open_questions.blocked_by: The pricer and the finite compiler's base case both charge a rank-one leaf; no cited text excludes or supplies a cheaper accounting.

open_questions.question: Does the hub rank law (Theorem 4) survive outside the coordinate-mask grammar, and is a half-width hub possible there?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The replays are gauge-equivalent to direct sums and cannot exhibit a non-gauge coupling; the proof carries the claim only inside the grammar.
open_questions.first_step: Find the weakest grammar change (non-coordinate masks, or two scalars per LOCAL) under which the Schur-complement and divisibility steps fail, then test a v = 2 instance.
open_questions.blocked_by: No exact decision tool outside coordinate masks.

open_questions.question: Does the form-capacity bound ku >= v extend to landings of down rows after X has reached V, and to targets with T[Y,Y] != 0?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A control family with such landings exceeds the bound, so the lemma is exactly as wide as the stated stop shape.
open_questions.first_step: Find the invariant that replaces the pi-rank count when a down row lands at a line, and check it on the control family.
open_questions.blocked_by: The numerical cells are generic-solution evidence only; unsolved cells are not evidence.
